intended_object: Given a commutative square g ∘ p = q ∘ f of continuous homomorphisms between compact Hausdorff abelian groups, this is the induced continuous homomorphism on cokernels Y / im f → Y' / im g, sending [y] to [q y]. Inferred from the docstring, the name and the simp lemma `quotientRangeMap_mk`.
explanation:
The body takes the composite Y → Y' → Y'/im g, i.e. the quotient map after q. It checks that im f lies in the kernel: by the square, q(f x) = g(p x), which lies in im g. It then lifts the composite through Y/im f with `QuotientAddGroup.lift`. Continuity holds because the quotient carries the coinduced topology and the composite is continuous. The result is the usual induced map on cokernels, [y] ↦ [q y], which is exactly what `quotientRangeMap_mk` states, holding by `rfl`.

The construction belongs to the library's own category `CompHausAddCommGrp`, where the quotient by the closed range is the cokernel object, so working in this setting is part of the definition's content. On the underlying groups, Mathlib's `QuotientAddGroup.map` is the same map without the topology. Nothing is restricted beyond what the setting requires, and there are no degenerate cases where it fails.
